revealWordProblem.title: (Review from 9.7) Apply: Treasure Map Mirror Twins
revealWordProblem.text: Captain Vega buries a chest at (-6, 4) on her treasure map. She wants to bury a decoy chest that is a mirror image of the real one, reflected across the y-axis, so raiders searching the wrong side will still find a clue. What are the coordinates of the decoy chest, and how far is it from the y-axis?
revealWordProblem.sampleAnswer: Reflecting across the y-axis flips the sign of the x-coordinate and keeps the y-coordinate the same, so (-6, 4) becomes (6, 4). The original chest is |-6| = 6 units from the y-axis, and the decoy is also 6 units from the y-axis, just on the opposite side. The decoy chest is at (6, 4), exactly 6 units from the y-axis.

vocabulary.definition: Any number you can write as a fraction. This includes fractions, decimals, and integers.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Cualquier número que puedes escribir como fracción. Incluye fracciones, decimales y enteros.

examples.why: It is written as a fraction.

vocabulary.definitionVi: Số có thể biểu diễn dưới dạng phân số của hai số nguyên.
vocabulary.definitionAr: عدد يمكن كتابته على شكل كسر يحتوي على بسط ومقام صحيحين.

vocabulary.definition: A number that shows part of a whole, like 3/4.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Un número que muestra una parte de un todo, como 3/4.

vocabulary.definitionAr: رقم يعبر عن أجزاء من الكل (مثال: a/b).

vocabulary.definition: One of the four parts of a coordinate grid, numbered I to IV.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Una de las cuatro partes de una cuadrícula de coordenadas, numeradas I a IV.
vocabulary.visual: I (+, +) top-right, II (-, +) top-left, III (-, -) bottom-left, IV (+, -) bottom-right

vocabulary.definitionAr: أحد الأجزاء الأربعة للمستوى الإحداثي الناتجة عن تقاطع المحورين.

vocabulary.definitionEs: Una coordenada menor que cero. Significa a la izquierda o debajo del centro.

vocabulary.definitionVi: Số âm dùng để chỉ vị trí trên trục của mặt phẳng tọa độ.

vocabulary.definition: How far apart two points are. It is never negative.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Qué tan separados están dos puntos. Nunca es negativo.

vocabulary.cloze: How far apart two points are on the coordinate plane is the ___.
vocabulary.definitionVi: Độ dài không gian giữa hai điểm.

vocabulary.definition: How far a number is from zero.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Qué tan lejos está un número de cero.

vocabulary.definitionVi: Khoảng cách từ một số đến số 0. Nó luôn luôn là số dương.
vocabulary.definitionAr: مسافة الرقم من الصفر. وهي دائماً موجبة.

vocabulary.definitionEs: Una imagen volteada de un punto al otro lado de una línea, a la misma distancia.

That is a slide, not a reflection.

vocabulary.definitionVi: Phép lật hình hoặc điểm qua một đường thẳng (trục đối xứng).

conceptIntro.heading: The Big Ideas — Lessons 9.4–9.7
conceptIntro.intro: Here is the one thing to remember from each lesson, plus a quick guided example. If one of these feels shaky, that lesson is right above this one in the menu — you can open it any time.
conceptIntro.keyIdea: 9.4: To plot a rational number, find the two whole numbers it falls between, then split the space into equal parts. • 9.5: The signs of (x, y) tell you the quadrant: (+,+) is I, (-,+) is II, (-,-) is III, (+,-) is IV. • 9.6: If points are on the same side of zero, subtract; if they are on opposite sides of zero, add the absolute values. • 9.7: Reflect over the x-axis: the y-coordinate changes sign. Reflect over the y-axis: the x-coordinate changes sign.

iDo.title: The Big Ideas (one per lesson)
lines: Lesson 9.4 — Rational Numbers on the Number Line: To plot a rational number, find the two whole numbers it falls between, then split the space into equal parts.
Lesson 9.5 — Ordered Pairs in All Four Quadrants: The signs of (x, y) tell you the quadrant: (+,+) is I, (-,+) is II, (-,-) is III, (+,-) is IV.
Lesson 9.6 — Distance on the Coordinate Plane: If points are on the same side of zero, subtract; if they are on opposite sides of zero, add the absolute values.
Lesson 9.7 — Reflect Points Across Axes: Reflect over the x-axis: the y-coordinate changes sign. Reflect over the y-axis: the x-coordinate changes sign.

weDo.title: Quick guided checks — one from each lesson
lines: From 9.4: Now let's plot 0.75. Which two whole numbers is it between? It is between 0 and 1.
From 9.5: Now let's plot (-5, 2). The x is -5, so which way do we move? Left 5 units.
From 9.6: Now let's find the distance from (1, -3) to (1, 5). What do these points share? The same x = 1, so it is a vertical line.
From 9.7: Now let's reflect (4, -5) over the x-axis. Which coordinate changes over the x-axis? The y-coordinate.

youDo.title: Show you're caught up
lines: The practice below mixes problems from Lessons 9.4–9.7. Each problem is tagged with its lesson number.
Stuck on one lesson's problems? Open that lesson from the curriculum menu for the full re-teach.

explore.instructions: Review from Lesson 9.7: Plot each original point and then plot its reflection across the given axis.
explore.label: Plot each point and its reflection. Verify the reflection rule.

discourse.prompt: What pattern do you notice about the coordinates when reflecting over the x-axis versus the y-axis?
discourse.sentenceFrame: When I reflect over the x-axis, the ___ -coordinate changes sign and the ___ -coordinate stays the same. When I reflect over the y-axis, the ___ -coordinate changes sign and the ___ -coordinate stays the same.

optional.stem: (Lesson 9.4) The first trail marker sits between 0 and 1. Which rational number belongs there?
optional.explanation: 3/4 = 0.75, which lands between 0 and 1. 1.5 and 2 are larger, and -1/2 is to the left of 0.
choiceFeedback: Double-check: verify the math step-by-step against the question.

optional.instructions: (Lesson 9.5) Captain Vega spotted four enemy ships. Drag each ship's coordinates into the correct quadrant of the map.
optional.hint: Arrange items step by step from first to last.

optional.stem: (Lesson 9.6) The Bank is at (2, 3) and the Library is at (2, 9). How many blocks apart are they?
optional.explanation: Same x = 2, so the segment is vertical. Distance = |9 - 3| = 6 blocks.
choiceFeedback: Double-check: verify the math step-by-step against the question.

optional.stem: (Lesson 9.7) Captain Vega folds the map along the x-axis. A marker at (7, 2) lands on its mirror image. What are the new coordinates?
optional.explanation: Folding along (reflecting across) the x-axis flips the sign of the y-coordinate only. (7, 2) becomes (7, -2).
choiceFeedback: Double-check: verify the math step-by-step against the question.

approaching.stem: (Lesson 9.4) Which point is located between -1 and -2 on the number line?
approaching.explanation: -1.5 is between -1 and -2 because it is 0.5 units to the left of -1 (or 0.5 units to the right of -2).
choiceFeedback: Double-check: verify the math step-by-step against the question.
hints: 'Between -1 and -2' is on the NEGATIVE side, in the gap from -1 to -2.
Turn each choice into a spot on the number line and check: is it past -1 but not past -2?
Start at -1 and move half a unit farther left. Which choice lands in that gap between -1 and -2?

choiceFeedback: Double-check: verify the math step-by-step against the question.
hints: Read 0.25 as a place-value number: 25 hundredths.
Write it as 25/100, then simplify by dividing the top and bottom by the same number.
Divide both 25 and 100 by 25. What simpler fraction do you get?

approaching.stem: (Lesson 9.5) In which quadrant is the point (-4, 5)?
approaching.explanation: The x-coordinate is negative (left) and the y-coordinate is positive (up). Left and up is Quadrant II.
choiceFeedback: Double-check: verify the math step-by-step against the question.
hints: Look at the signs: x = -4 is negative and y = 5 is positive.
Negative x means move LEFT; positive y means move UP. Ask which corner of the plane is left-and-up.
From the origin, slide left 4 and climb up 5. Quadrants count I, II, III, IV counterclockwise from top-right.

approaching.stem: (Lesson 9.5) A point has a positive x-coordinate and a negative y-coordinate. Which quadrant is it in?
approaching.explanation: Positive x (right) and negative y (down) = Quadrant IV (bottom-right).
choiceFeedback: Double-check: verify the math step-by-step against the question.
hints: Positive x pushes you RIGHT; negative y drops you DOWN.
Find the corner that is right of the y-axis and below the x-axis. Quadrants I–IV go counterclockwise from top-right.
Try a sample point like (3, -2): go right 3, then down 2. See which corner of the grid that lands in.

approaching.stem: (Lesson 9.6) What is the distance between (-4, 3) and (2, 3)?
approaching.explanation: Both points have y = 3, so this is a horizontal distance. |2 - (-4)| = |2 + 4| = 6 units.
choiceFeedback: Double-check: verify the math step-by-step against the question.
hints: Both points have y = 3, so they sit on the same horizontal line — only the x-values differ.
Find the gap between x = -4 and x = 2. The path crosses zero, so add the two distances |-4| and |2|.
Count from -4 to 0 (that's 4 units), then from 0 to 2. Add the two parts together.

approaching.stem: (Lesson 9.6) What is the distance between (5, -2) and (5, 4)?
approaching.explanation: Both points have x = 5, so this is a vertical distance. |4 - (-2)| = |4 + 2| = 6 units.
choiceFeedback: Double-check: verify the math step-by-step against the question.
hints: Both points share x = 5 — the segment is VERTICAL, so compare the y-values -2 and 4.
The path crosses zero: split it into a below-zero part and an above-zero part using absolute values.
From y = -2 up to 0 is 2 units; from 0 up to 4 is 4 more. Add the parts.

approaching.stem: (Lesson 9.7) What is the reflection of (4, -3) over the x-axis?
approaching.explanation: Reflecting over the x-axis changes the sign of the y-coordinate. The x stays the same (4), and the y changes from -3 to 3. The answer is (4, 3).
choiceFeedback: Double-check: verify the math step-by-step against the question.
hints: Reflecting over the x-axis flips the point UP/DOWN — the left/right position doesn't move.
Keep the x-coordinate the same and switch the sign of the y-coordinate. Don't swap the numbers' order.
The point sits 3 units below the x-axis. Its mirror sits the same 3 units above, with the x still 4.

approaching.stem: (Lesson 9.7) What is the reflection of (-2, 6) over the y-axis?
approaching.explanation: Reflecting over the y-axis changes the sign of the x-coordinate. x goes from -2 to 2, and y stays 6. The answer is (2, 6).
choiceFeedback: Double-check: verify the math step-by-step against the question.
hints: Reflecting over the y-axis flips LEFT/RIGHT — the height stays the same.
Switch the sign of the x-coordinate and keep the y-coordinate 6 unchanged.
The point is 2 units left of the y-axis. Its mirror lands 2 units to the RIGHT, at the same height.

onLevel.label: (Lesson 9.4) Plot these rational numbers: -3.5, -1/4, 2.75, -2, 1 1/2
onLevel.hint: Try the first step of the solution process.
hints: Mixed forms here — turn every number into a decimal first: -1/4 and 1 1/2 both need converting.
-1/4 = -0.25 and 1 1/2 = 1.5. Then place each one: whole part first, then the extra fraction of a unit.
Plot A at -3.5: go to -3, then half a tick farther left. Then plot D at -2, right on its whole-number tick.

onLevel.instructions: (Lesson 9.4) Convert between fraction and decimal form. Then plot on a mental number line to compare.
onLevel.hint: Complete each row by converting the description to (x, y) form.
hints: Each row needs the same number in two forms, plus the two integers it sits between.
Fraction to decimal: divide top by bottom. Decimal to fraction: use place value (0.6 = six tenths). Keep negatives negative.
Row 1: divide 3 by 4 to get the decimal. Then ask: is that result more than 0 and less than 1?

onLevel.label: (Lesson 9.5) Plot one point in each quadrant: (3, 2), (-4, 1), (-2, -3), (5, -4)
onLevel.hint: Plot each point by moving right first, then up from the origin.
hints: Signs steer you: positive x goes right, negative x goes left, positive y goes up, negative y goes down.
For each point, do the x move first (left/right), then the y move (up/down). The label tells you which quadrant to expect.
Plot (3, 2) first: right 3, up 2 — the top-right region. Then (-4, 1): LEFT 4, then up 1.

onLevel.instructions: (Lesson 9.5) For each ordered pair, write the signs of x and y and name the quadrant (or axis).
onLevel.hint: Complete each row by converting the description to (x, y) form.
hints: Each row asks for the sign of x, the sign of y, then the quadrant those signs give — or an axis if a coordinate is 0.
Sign map: (+, +) I, (-, +) II, (-, -) III, (+, -) IV. A 0 for x means y-axis; a 0 for y means x-axis.
Row 1: decide if 6 is positive or negative, then -2. Write both signs, then look the pair up on the sign map.

onLevel.label: (Lesson 9.6) Plot these pairs and find each distance: A(-5, 3) to B(2, 3), and C(4, -2) to D(4, 4)
onLevel.hint: Plot each point by moving right first, then up from the origin.
hints: A and B share y = 3 (a horizontal pair); C and D share x = 4 (a vertical pair).
Plot all four, then count grid squares along each segment — or add absolute values when a segment crosses an axis.
Plot A: LEFT 5, up 3. Plot B: right 2, up 3. The AB distance is the count between x = -5 and x = 2.

onLevel.instructions: (Lesson 9.6) Find the perimeter of each rectangle using its vertex coordinates.
onLevel.hint: Complete each row by converting the description to (x, y) form.
hints: Each rectangle's width comes from its two different x-values; the height comes from its two different y-values.
Width = |bigger x − smaller x|, height works the same with y's. Then perimeter = 2 × (width + height).
Rect 1: the x-values are -3 and 4. Count from -3 to 4 (crossing zero: 3 + 4). Then find the height from 1 and 5.

onLevel.label: (Lesson 9.7) Plot (1, 4) and its reflections: over the x-axis, over the y-axis, and over both axes
onLevel.hint: Plot each point by moving right first, then up from the origin.
hints: Each reflection flips exactly one thing: x-axis flips the y sign; y-axis flips the x sign; both axes flip both.
Start from (1, 4) each time. Write the three mirror pairs on paper first, then plot all four points.
Plot the original: right 1, up 4. For 'over x-axis,' keep x = 1 and flip the y's sign — straight below it.

onLevel.instructions: (Lesson 9.7) Find the reflection of each point over the given axis.
onLevel.hint: Complete each row by converting the description to (x, y) form.
hints: The axis column tells you which coordinate flips: x-axis flips the y; y-axis flips the x. The other number stays.
Copy the original pair, change only ONE sign, and keep the coordinates in the same order. Watch the rows with a 0.
Row 1: (3, -7) over the x-axis — keep the 3, flip the sign of -7, and write the new pair in (x, y) order.

extending.title: (Lesson 9.4) Find the Plotting Error

workedExample.label: Student thinking
workedExample.work: -3/4 has a 3 and a 4, so I go to -3 on the number line and then count 4 more to the left

extending.correctWork: -3/4 means negative three-fourths, which is 3/4 of the way from 0 toward -1. It should be plotted between 0 and -1, not at -7. The student treated the numerator and denominator as separate whole numbers.
hints: What does the fraction 3/4 actually mean? How much of a whole is it?
-3/4 is a number between 0 and -1. It is 3/4 of one unit to the left of zero.

extending.title: (Lesson 9.5) Find the Quadrant Error

workedExample.label: Student thinking
workedExample.work: The x is -3, so I go left 3. The y is -5, so I go up 5.

extending.correctWork: A negative y-coordinate means DOWN, not up. Go left 3 and DOWN 5. The point (-3, -5) is in Quadrant III (both negative), not Quadrant II.
hints: What direction does a NEGATIVE y-coordinate go — up or down?
Both coordinates are negative. In which quadrant are both x and y negative?

extending.title: (Lesson 9.6) Find the Distance Error
extending.correctWork: The student subtracted 5 - 3, but the first x-coordinate is -3, not 3. The correct calculation is |5 - (-3)| = |5 + 3| = 8 units. When points span opposite sides of an axis, you must add the absolute values: |-3| + |5| = 3 + 5 = 8.
hints: The student dropped the negative sign on -3. What is the actual difference between -3 and 5?
Try counting on the number line from -3 to 5. How many units is that?

extending.title: (Lesson 9.7) Find the Reflection Error

workedExample.label: Student thinking
workedExample.work: The y-axis is vertical, so I change the y-coordinate

extending.correctWork: Reflecting over the y-axis changes the x-coordinate, not the y-coordinate. The correct reflection of (-3, 5) over the y-axis is (3, 5). The student confused which coordinate changes for each axis.
hints: The y-AXIS is the vertical line. Points flip ACROSS it, meaning they move left/right. Which coordinate controls left/right?
Over the y-axis: change x. Over the x-axis: change y. The name of the axis tells you which coordinate STAYS the same.

optionalActivity.name: Catch-Up Challenge
optionalActivity.intro: Mix it up: pick the right lesson's big idea for each problem — that's the real catch-up skill.

practice.commonMistake: A common mistake in Reflect Points Across Axes is flipping the sign of the wrong coordinate — changing the x-coordinate when reflecting over the x-axis, instead of the y-coordinate (or vice versa for the y-axis). For example, to reflect (3, -5) over the x-axis, a student might flip the x-coordinate and write (-3, -5), but reflecting over the x-axis only changes the sign of the y-coordinate: (3, -5) becomes (3, 5). Before you submit, ask: 'Did I flip the sign of the coordinate that matches the axis I'm reflecting over — y for the x-axis, x for the y-axis?'

diagram.title: Symmetric Enemy Ship Placement
diagram.caption: The ship sits at (3, 2); reflecting over the y-axis flips x to (-3, 2) and reflecting over the x-axis flips y to (3, -2) — each enemy is the same distance across its axis.

connect.scenario: A game designer creates a spaceship at (3, 2) and wants to place enemy ships as reflections to make the level symmetric. One enemy is reflected over the y-axis, and another is reflected over the x-axis.
connect.promptQuestion: How do reflections help the game designer create a balanced, symmetric level?
connect.prompt: The enemy reflected over the y-axis is at ___ because ___. The enemy reflected over the x-axis is at ___ because ___. Reflections help game designers because ___.

exitTicket.stem: (Catch-up check, from Lesson 9.5) A point has a negative x-coordinate and a negative y-coordinate. Which quadrant is it in?
exitTicket.explanation: Quadrant III is where both x and y are negative. This means the point is left of the origin and below the origin.
choiceFeedback: Quadrant I has both positive — you need both negative.
Quadrant II has negative x but positive y — check the y sign.
Quadrant IV has positive x — you need x negative too.
hints: Negative x and negative y — think about which direction each sign pushes the point.
Negative x means LEFT of the y-axis; negative y means BELOW the x-axis. Find the region that is both.
Plot a sample like (-4, -5): left 4, down 5. Count quadrants counterclockwise from top-right to name it.
